Wait, let me reconsider. The cells at rows 39-43, cols 24-28 and 34-38 are "open" (not black), but maybe they're not the right color for the squares to move there. The squares are sky blue (S), and they seem to only move within corridors that match their "track" or "path".
Actually, looking more carefully at the maze structure, I notice the corridors have different colors:
- Left side corridors are yellow (Y)
- Right side corridors are orange (O)
- Mixed corridors have both colors
The blue squares might only be able to move within corridors of a specific color, or they might need to follow a specific path.
Wait, but the first UP move DID work - the squares moved from rows 49-53 to 44-48. Let me check what color the corridors were at rows 44-48 and rows 49-53.
Actually, let me reconsider the whole movement system. Maybe the squares don't move freely through all corridors. Maybe they only move along specific tracks or paths.
Let me look at the initial state more carefully. The blue squares started at rows 49-53. Looking at the corridor data:
- Rows 49-53: cols 29-33 (5 wide)
- Rows 44-48: cols 19-23, 29-33, 39-43
Wait, the initial blue squares were at cols 19-23 and 39-43, but the corridor data for rows 49-53 only shows cols 29-33. That's contradictory. Unless the blue squares themselves are considered corridor cells (they're S, not B).
Let me re-examine. The corridor cells include Y, O, and S. So the blue squares ARE part of the corridor. The corridor at rows 49-53 includes the blue squares at cols 19-23 and 39-43, plus the center at cols 29-33.
So the full corridor at rows 49-53 is: cols 19-23 (S), 29-33 (O/Y), 39-43 (S).
And at rows 44-48: cols 19-23, 29-33, 39-43.
Now, the UP move from rows 49-53 to 44-48 worked. But the UP move from rows 44-48 to 39-43 didn't work, even though the path seems open.
Wait, maybe the issue is that the squares need to be at specific columns to move vertically. Let me check: at rows 39-43, the corridor is cols 24-43 (20 wide). The squares are at cols 24-28 and 34-38, which are within this range. But maybe the squares can only move vertically when they're at the "center" of a corridor section, or when they're at a specific column.
Hmm, let me think about this differently. Maybe the squares can only move vertically through the center corridor (cols 29-33). Let me check:
- At rows 44-48, there's a center corridor at cols 29-33
- The squares are at cols 24-28 and 34-38, not at the center
- Maybe they need to be at cols 29-33 to move UP
Let me try moving RIGHT again to bring both squares to cols 29-33, then try UP.
Actually wait, RIGHT moves the left square right and the right square left. So from cols 24-28 and 34-38, RIGHT would move them to cols 29-33 and 29-33. Both squares would be at the same position!
Let me try that.

<function=python>

# Hypothesis: H1 | Two 5x5 blue squares move in a maze. LEFT/RIGHT moves them horizontally in opposite directions, UP/DOWN moves both vertically. Squares can only move vertically through the center corridor (cols 29-33).
#

    print(f"Blue squares after UP: rows {min(rows2)}-{max(rows2)}, cols {min(cols2)}-{max(cols2)}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
